note: The single source of truth for the BeatBox bridge. Rust generates its
types from it (crates/contract/build.rs); TypeScript mirrors it in
web/src/bridge/types.ts, and web/tests/contract.test.mjs checks that
mirror. Neither side hand-writes the other's shape, and an action that
exists on only one side fails a test rather than a user.
Field names are snake_case here because that is what the engine speaks.
The wire is camelCase: the conversion is mechanical (crates/contract's
door), so there is no hand-written mapping anywhere and no drift to keep
in sync.
Type language: str | int | float | bool | any, a PascalCase type name from
'types', '[]' for a list, '?' for optional. Nothing else is allowed.
An action marked `mutates` changes the world: it starts containers, spends
points, or tears an environment down. Nothing may call one speculatively --
a test that looped over every action and dispatched it is how four
containers and a network ended up orphaned on a developer's machine.
An action in the `host.` namespace is declared here and answered by the
window rather than by the daemon: the window closing is the person's,
not the machine's. It is still one door -- the page calls it like any
other action.
`answered_by` says which half of BeatBox answers an action or says an
event: `daemon` for the machine the
sandboxes run on, `shell` for the person at the screen -- their files,
their language, the window closing. The page never needs to know; the
shell routes by it.

system.probe.summary: What this machine can actually run, and where BeatBox keeps things.

system.locale.summary: The active language and every beatbox.* string in it.

system.set_language.summary: Switch the language of the whole application.

system.preferences.summary: The person's few choices: what closing does to running machines (ask | stop | leave), whether the rail shows the builder's pages, and what a new machine starts with.

system.set_preferences.summary: Change those choices, and remember them for the next window.

system.about.summary: Which BeatBox this is, the engine running the machines, and where its folder and log are.

host.reveal.summary: Open BeatBox's folder or the engine's log with this computer's own program for it: folder | log.

storage.usage.summary: What BeatBox keeps on this computer's disk: each machine, each disk and who it is made into, the guest tools, and rooms left by machines that are gone.

storage.sweep.summary: Remove the rooms left by machines that are gone, as a start does. Nothing a machine BeatBox knows still uses.

jobs.current.summary: The job that is already in flight, if any -- so a screen that mounts partway through one (a tab switched away and back) can learn about it without waiting for the next event, which may be a while yet.

host.closing.summary: Answer the question the window asked on its way out: stop | leave | cancel.

host.display.summary: Open or focus the BeatBox-owned window that shows a running machine.

files.places.summary: The folders the chooser offers as one click. Only ones that exist.

files.list.summary: What is in one folder. `suffixes` is space-separated and empty means everything.

files.read.summary: A small text file the person chose in the chooser, as text: up to 4 MB.

sandbox.types.summary: Which kinds of sandbox this build can make.

sandbox.list.summary: Every sandbox that exists, oldest first.

sandbox.view.summary: One sandbox, whole, from what is already known.

sandbox.refresh.summary: Go and ask the provider what is true now.

sandbox.create.summary: Make a sandbox of a registered type.

sandbox.transition.summary: start, stop, pause, resume, reset or destroy.

sandbox.act.summary: Ask a sandbox to do one of the things it declared.

sandbox.events.summary: What was said after a given sequence number.

disks.list.summary: The disks BeatBox has made, newest first.

beatdrop.inspect.summary: Physical Linux disks with every mountpoint below them, and the filesystems on other disks a live capture can write to.

beatdrop.start.summary: Copy a physical Linux disk into a private raw base image; a disk in use is rebuilt file by file onto a target on another disk.

beatdrop.folders.summary: The folders inside one (the home folder when empty) with what each holds, largest first, for choosing what a live capture leaves out.

beatdrop.measure.summary: Bytes a folder or file on a disk in use holds, for leaving it out of a live capture.

beatdrop.cancel.summary: Cancel the active physical disk capture, if there is one.

disks.build.summary: Make an empty disk and boot an installer disc at it. Unattended, it ends at the first reboot, and a Windows disc installs without a window. With a machine (as sandbox.create takes it), that machine is made from the disk and started; the job then answers with its id. Answers with a job.

disks.finish.summary: Say the install is done: ask its guest to shut down, and end the job.

sandbox.rename.summary: Call a machine or a network something else, in any state. Only its name changes.

sandbox.reconfigure.summary: New processors, memory and settings for a machine that is off. Answers with the machine.

sandbox.use.summary: Point a sandbox that is off at other sandboxes (a server's machine and network). Answers with the sandbox.

tools.status.summary: Whether the Windows guest tools are here, and how big fetching them is.

tools.fetch.summary: Download the pinned Windows guest tools, once. Answers with a job.

tools.insert.summary: Plug the guest tools into a running machine as a read-only USB drive.

disks.inspect.summary: What a disk is and whether a machine can be made of it: its format, size and firmware, VirtualBox snapshots beside it, and for an .ova the disk inside.

disks.unpack.summary: Take the disk out of an .ova into the disks folder, as a job that answers with where it went.

setup.status.summary: What BeatBox needs from this computer, whether each is here, and whether BeatBox can put it here itself.

setup.fix.summary: Put one missing thing in place: qemu | acceleration | guest_tools. Asks for the system's own password or approval. Answers with a job.

disks.forget.summary: Delete a disk BeatBox made. Answers with what is left.

commands.list.summary: The commands kept for running inside machines: every global one, and each machine's own.

commands.save.summary: Keep a command, new or changed. `machine` empty keeps it for every machine. Answers with them all.

commands.forget.summary: Stop keeping a command. Answers with what is left.

watchers.list.summary: Every watcher: a line run again and again inside a machine, and what it last answered.

watchers.save.summary: Start a watcher, or change one (its line, how often, when it tells, paused or not). Answers with them all.

watchers.forget.summary: Stop and forget a watcher. Answers with what is left.

job.summary: Progress on work that outlives the request that asked for it.

locale.summary: The language changed; every screen re-reads its text.

closing.summary: The window is trying to close and something is still up. Ask, then answer with host.closing.

sandbox.summary: A sandbox said something: a lifecycle change, an action, or a fact from inside.
